facts.name: Catalog heading and plan codes
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 University Catalog program heading is Computer Engineering, M.S. The page also lists Academic Plan Codes for SDSU Global Campus and SDSU Global Campus-Flex.
facts.quote: Computer Engineering, M.S. (Major Code: 09094) (Academic Plan Code: 445003MSS) (Academic Plan Code: 445004MSE - SDSU Global Campus) (Academic Plan Code: 445004MSF - SDSU Global Campus-Flex)

facts.name: Four focus areas
facts.detail: The department offers the M.S. in computer engineering with graduate courses in Computer Networks, Embedded Systems, VLSI systems, and Machine Learning/Scientific Computing.
facts.quote: The program seeks to provide students with core knowledge through graduate courses offered in the four focus areas of Computer Networks, Embedded Systems, Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) systems and Machine Learning/ Scientific Computing.

facts.name: Admission GPA by student type
facts.detail: The catalog asks for a bachelor's in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or a closely related area, with a GPA of 3.0 or better for international students and 2.85 for domestic students, on a 4.0 scale. An earlier department-page fact described the 2.85 figure as applying to the last 60 semester units of technical coursework; this catalog sentence does not add that restriction. Both quotes are kept and no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or closely related areas with a grade point average of 3.0 or better for international students and a minimum grade point average of 2.85 for domestic students, based on 4.0 scale;

facts.name: International English scores
facts.detail: International students must have a minimum TOEFL score of 85 or a minimum IELTS score of 6.5.
facts.quote: A minimum TOEFL score of 85 or a minimum IELTS score of 6.5 for international students;

facts.name: GRE scores required on this catalog page
facts.detail: This 2026-2027 catalog admissions list includes official GRE scores. The department admissions page fact f23 quotes 'GRE scores are not required.' Both quotes are kept and no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Submission of the official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores;

facts.name: One letter of recommendation
facts.detail: The catalog admissions list requires one letter of recommendation.
facts.quote: One letter of recommendation.

facts.name: 30 units with at least 15 at the 600 or 700 level
facts.detail: The degree requires 30 units of 500-, 600-, or 700-level courses, including at least 15 units of 600- or 700-level coursework. An earlier department-page fact said 18 of the 30 units should be 600- and 700-numbered courses. Both quotes are kept and no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Completion of 30 units of 500-, 600-, or 700-level courses to include at least 15 units of 600 or 700 level coursework.

facts.name: Plan A thesis or Plan B project
facts.detail: Students must have a graduate-advisor-approved program of study that meets core, depth, and breadth requirements, and must choose Plan A (Thesis) or Plan B (Project).
facts.quote: Students must also choose one of two pathways: Plan A (Thesis) or Plan B (Project), for degree completion.

facts.name: Depth and breadth areas
facts.detail: Students select a depth area and complete approved courses from that area, plus a set of approved courses from other areas in consultation with the graduate advisor. In this paragraph the page names the areas Computer Networks, Embedded operating systems, Machine Learning and Scientific Computing, and VLSI Circuit Design.
facts.quote: The offered areas are Computer Networks, Embedded operating systems, Machine Learning and Scientific Computing and VLSI Circuit Design.

facts.name: Computer Networks core choice
facts.detail: For the Computer Networks area, students take one of COMPE 560, E E 602, or E E 603 as core, and at least 3 courses from the Computer Networks depth list.
facts.quote: Students are required to take one of these courses as core: COMPE 560 - Computer and Data Networks Units: 3 or E E 602 - Stochastic Signals and Systems Units: 3 or E E 603 - Engineering Optimization Units: 3

facts.name: Embedded Systems core
facts.detail: For Embedded Systems, students take the core course COMPE 571 and at least 3 courses from that area's depth list.
facts.quote: Embedded Systems Students are required to take the core course: COMPE 571 - Embedded Operating Systems Units: 3

facts.name: Machine Learning and Scientific Computing core
facts.detail: For Machine Learning and Scientific Computing, students take the core course COMPE 510 and at least 3 courses from that area's depth list. The catalog text repeats the word 'the' in this sentence; the quote is kept as written.
facts.quote: Machine Learning and Scientific Computing Students are required to take the the core course: COMPE 510 - Machine Learning for Engineers Units: 3

facts.name: VLSI Systems core
facts.detail: For VLSI Systems, students take the core course COMPE 572 and at least 3 courses from that area's depth list.
facts.quote: VLSI Systems Students are required to take the core course: COMPE 572 - VLSI Circuit Design Units: 3

facts.name: Depth-course minimum of three
facts.detail: In each depth area, the page says students must take at least 3 of the listed depth courses.
facts.quote: Students must take at least 3 of these courses:

facts.name: Plan A thesis units
facts.detail: Plan A students take COMPE 797 Research for 6 units and COMPE 799A Thesis for 3 units. Credit for COMPE 797 is given only after COMPE 799A is successfully completed.
facts.quote: Requirements for Plan A (Thesis) Students are required to take COMPE 797 - Research Units: 3-6 (6 units) Cr/NC/RP COMPE 799A - Thesis Units: 3 (3 units)

facts.name: COMPE 797 credit after thesis
facts.detail: Credit for COMPE 797 is given only after the student successfully completes COMPE 799A.
facts.quote: Credit for COMPE 797 will be given only after successfully completing COMPE 799A.

facts.name: Plan B project timing and course
facts.detail: Plan B students may enroll in COMPE 798 after 18 units, but must do so in the semester immediately after completing 27 units. The project is 3 units of COMPE 798 Special Study, graded Cr/NC/RP. The department determines the evaluation process, enforced by the graduate advisor.
facts.quote: Students may enroll in the project course, COMPE 798 after completion of 18 units, but must do so in the semester immediately following completion of 27 units.
